title: Traveler Profile

intelligence.label: Travel Intelligence
intelligence.text: Couple (traveler + wife) · China  → Vietnam · September 1–14, 2026 (14 days). Budget $20,000 USD for both travelers. Constraint: Avoid peak tourist hours.

metrics.label: Physical
metrics.value: Both travelers in excellent physical condition

seasonality.caption: Seasonality scorecard
seasonality.summary: September balances heat constraints with beach time in Vietnam and shoulder pricing in China.

validations.text: September in both China and Vietnam means heat + humidity + possible typhoon/rain — itinerary must have strong rainy-day fallbacks
Vietnam resort stay should be clustered for relaxation (not fragmented across cities)
China portion should prioritize efficiency: maximize cultural/shopping value without over-scheduling
HKG entry → high-speed rail to Guangzhou for mainland China segment; then flight to Vietnam (no overland China–Vietnam border)
Hong Kong and mainland China are separate immigration regimes — plan visas and apps for both

intro: - Style: Relaxed, culturally immersive — not rushed, not spontaneous - Pace: Moderate-relaxed; late mornings preferred; long transit days should be avoided - Ideal day: Late brunch → beach or waterfront walk → scenic nature views of the city at dusk

tables.caption: Budget
rows: Splurge in Vietnam; be value-conscious in China

tables.caption: Deal-Breakers
rows: Avoid peak tourist hours; book early-entry tickets; skip hyper-popular queues
September is shoulder/late-monsoon season — heat is a real concern in both countries. Schedule outdoor activities for early morning or late afternoon. Midday rests essential.

bullets.heading: Style & Pace
items: Style: Relaxed, culturally immersive — not rushed, not spontaneous
Pace: Moderate-relaxed; late mornings preferred; long transit days should be avoided
Ideal day: Late brunch → beach or waterfront walk → scenic nature views of the city at dusk

bullets.heading: Accommodation
items: Tier: 4–5 star hotels; resorts acceptable and preferred in Vietnam
Booking requirement: Must be bookable on US platforms (Marriott, Hilton, Expedia, Hotels.com, Booking.com)
No: hostels, guesthouses, Airbnb with uncertain quality

bullets.heading: Physical Profile
items: Both travelers in excellent physical condition
Can handle moderate walking, stairs, uneven terrain

bullets.heading: Transit Experience & Preferences
items: Local mass transit (metro/subway): positive past experience — recommended
Taxis: past negative experience (rip-offs) — avoid unmetered taxis; use apps (DiDi in China, Grab in Vietnam)
